{"status": "success", "output": "===== README.md =====
1|# FairFahren 🚕
2|
3|A tiny procedural 3D driving game: steer a German taxi through a generated slice of Berlin.
4|**~52 KB of plain JavaScript. No assets. No dependencies. No build step.** Every street, building, tree and landmark comes from one seed.
5|
6|Built as the base project for developer interviews: candidates extend it (see [the candidate brief](docs/04-candidate-brief.md)).
7|
8|## Quick start
9|
10|Requires Node 22+ and a browser with WebGL2.
11|
12|```bash
13|npm start
14|```
15|
16|Open <http://localhost:8080>. Add `?seed=42` for a different city.
17|
18|| Key | Action |
19||---|---|
20|| W / ↑ | accelerate |
21|| S / ↓ | brake, then reverse |
22|| A / ← · D / → | steer |
23|| Space | handbrake |
24|| C | camera: chase → bonnet → overhead |
25|| R | reset to spawn |
26|
27|## What's in the city
28|
29|Berlin street grid with real street names · *Altbau* perimeter blocks with courtyards, shop fronts and vacant lots · *Plattenbau* slabs (more in the east) · parks · the Spree with bridges and *Ufer* streets · *Unter den Linden* with a linden-tree median · a city gate you can drive through · a TV tower on a plaza.
30|
31|## Checks
32|
33|```bash
34|npm test
35|```
36|
37|```bash
38|npm run size
39|```
40|
41|`npm run check` runs both. The size budget (96 KB raw / 32 KB gzip for `index.html` + `src/`) is enforced.
42|
43|## Project layout
44|
45|```
46|index.html            page, HUD, loads src/main.js
47|src/main.js           wiring + fixed-timestep game loop
48|src/core/             seeded RNG, math (matrices)
49|src/gfx/              mesh builder, shaders, WebGL2 renderer
50|src/world/            city generator (pure data) + city mesh
51|src/vehicle/          taxi physics, collision, taxi model
52|src/game/             input, camera, HUD
53|test/                 node --test unit tests
54|tools/                dev server, size check
55|docs/                 requirements, spec, setup, candidate brief, interviewer guide, ADRs
56|```
57|
58|## Documentation
59|
60|1. [Requirements](docs/01-requirements.md)
61|2. [Technical specification](docs/02-technical-specification.md)
62|3. [Prerequisites & setup](docs/03-prerequisites.md)
63|4. [Candidate brief](docs/04-candidate-brief.md)
64|5. [Interviewer guide](docs/05-interviewer-guide.md) — confidential, remove before sharing
65|6. Architecture decisions: [raw WebGL2](docs/adr/0001-raw-webgl2-no-engine.md) · [seeded generation](docs/adr/0002-seeded-procedural-generation.md) · [size budget](docs/adr/000
===== docs/adr/0003-size-budget.md =====
1|# ADR 0003 — An enforced size budget
2|
3|**Status:** accepted · **Date:** 2026-11-04
4|
5|## Context
6|"Kilobytes, not megabytes" is the core constraint of the project. Unenforced budgets erode one commit at a time.
7|
8|## Decision
9|`tools/size-check.mjs` measures the shipped files (`index.html` + `src/**`) concatenated, raw and gzip level 9, and fails above **96 KB raw / 32 KB gzip**. It runs as `npm run size` and is part of `npm run check`.
10|
11|The MVP uses ~52 KB raw / ~19 KB gzip, leaving ~40 % headroom for candidate features. Source is shipped unminified so candidates and reviewers can read it; comments count against the budget on purpose (it rewards concise code, not deleted documentation — the gzip limit is the one that matters).
12|
13|## Consequences
14|- ✅ The constraint is objective and visible in CI or pre-commit.
15|- ✅ Discussions about bytes become concrete ("this feature costs 2.1 KB gzip").
16|- ❌ Raw size penalises comments; if this becomes a problem, add a minify step and budget the minified output instead.
===== docs/adr/0001-raw-webgl2-no-engine.md =====
1|# ADR 0001 — Raw WebGL2 instead of a 3D engine
2|
3|**Status:** accepted · **Date:** 2026-11-04
4|
5|## Context
6|The game must ship in kilobytes (NFR-01) with zero dependencies (NFR-03), and candidates should be able to read *all* of the code. Engines like three.js (600+ KB minified), Babylon.js or Unity WebGL builds are megabytes.
7|
8|## Decision
9|Use the browser's WebGL2 API directly with one small renderer (`src/gfx/renderer.js`, ~3.5 KB) and one shader program. Geometry is built on the CPU with `MeshBuilder`.
10|
11|## Consequences
12|- ✅ The whole engine layer (`src/core` + `src/gfx`) is ~16 KB of commented, readable source; no build step, no `node_modules`.
13|- ✅ Candidates see every layer — a good test of fundamentals (matrices, buffers, shaders).
14|- ❌ No scene graph, materials system, shadows or picking out of the box; features like these must be written (and can be interview tasks).
15|- ❌ WebGL2 only — no WebGL1 fallback (acceptable: all evergreen browsers support it).
===== docs/adr/0002-seeded-procedural-generation.md =====
1|# ADR 0002 — Everything is generated from one seed
2|
3|**Status:** accepted · **Date:** 2026-11-04
4|
5|## Context
6|No asset files are allowed (NFR-02), yet the city must look like Berlin and be the same for every player and every test run (NFR-05).
7|
8|## Decision
9|- One 32-bit seed drives a mulberry32 PRNG (`src/core/rng.js`).
10|- Features draw from **forked** streams (`rng.fork('trees')`, `fork('block:3,2')`) so that changing one feature does not reshuffle the rest of the world.
11|- Generation produces **plain data** (`generateCity`) that is separately turned into geometry (`buildCityMesh`) and colliders — so it is testable in Node.
12|- Surface detail (windows, water, asphalt) is generated in the fragment shader from world position instead of textures.
13|- `Math.random()` is banned for world content.
14|
15|## Consequences
16|- ✅ A city costs 4 bytes of "content"; any seed is shareable via `?seed=`.
17|- ✅ World invariants can be unit-tested across many seeds.
18|- ❌ "Berlin" is approximated by rules (block structure, river, landmarks, names), not by real map data.
19|- ❌ Designers cannot hand-place things; any hand-made feature must be expressed as a rule.
